impact.rationale: The patch changes a root/unshare CI lane and its bounded public failure artifact schema. A defect could hide or misclassify CI failure progress, but it does not alter product Go bytes, production state, authorization, or runtime success criteria.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The change is limited to CI diagnostics, uses exact closed enums and source-bound monotonic records, preserves the prior 40-name capture set, and passed 58 directly relevant synthetic tests plus independent source-closure checks. Real Linux namespace execution remains a downstream check.

regressionProtection.rationale: Direct tests cover short reads, named replacement, marker tampering, all phases, exception categories, capture names, secret sentinels, nested classification equality, and nonzero failure behavior. Bash syntax and 841-path source closure also passed, but no real Linux namespace or Go suite was run in this review.

recoverability.rationale: The patch changes only ten CI, diagnostic, contract, and test files, introduces no migration or persistent product format, and can be reverted as one source change.

confidence.rationale: Patch identity, byte closure, privacy projection, callers, and focused tests are fully evidenced. Confidence is limited by the intentionally absent Linux namespace and exact candidate CI execution.

applicability.rationale: The failed exact-747 joint lane currently publishes only SCENE_FAILED counts and hashes; the changed workflow, namespace harness, runner, and sanitizer are the owned path that produces that artifact.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: Without this change, another scene failure remains unable to distinguish namespace, isolation, prepare, fixture, B0, J1, R2, finalization, or private sanitizer progress, causing repeated blind diagnosis.

riskDrivers: The lane uses root, unshare, mounts, UID transition, and Linux-only namespace behavior.
The safe-failure public schema changes from v2 to v3 for scene failures.
Runner and checker now consume one shared authoritative 40-name capture set.
No exact candidate Linux namespace or Go execution was performed.
protectiveFactors: Every public diagnostic is selected from a closed enum; exception messages and raw type names are never serialized.
Private progress uses source-bound fixed-name O_EXCL records, stable readback, monotonic order, and bounded size.
Invalid, missing, replaced, extra, or source-mismatched records degrade to bounded UNKNOWN values.
The failure card remains status FAIL and cannot claim runtime acceptance.
The candidate capture-name set is exactly equal to the prior checker set of 40 names.
P207 workflow and source-contract blobs are unchanged.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Exception messages, paths, URLs, headers, bodies, tokens, and private files never enter the public failure card.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A PermissionError containing an Authorization token and private path is serialized via str(error) or a raw class name.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: exception_type maps ordered builtin classes to fixed categories, Failure stores only a validated code, capture names come from a fixed set, and tests inject secret sentinels and assert none appear in the bounded card.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Published progress is an exact source-bound monotonic prefix and cannot be forged by missing, duplicate, out-of-order, symlinked, hardlinked, oversized, short-read, or replaced records.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A named file is replaced between lstat and read or a later phase marker appears without its predecessor.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: _private_read compares named/opened/after identities including ctime, _progress_rows requires exact fixed names and prefix order, and invalid evidence returns the all-UNKNOWN classification.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Diagnostic publication never turns a failing scene into success or weakens existing acceptance.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: joint workflow, ci_namespace.sh finish, and safe failure schema
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A successfully written diagnostic card causes the Real scene step or job to return zero or claims runtimeAcceptanceProven.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The namespace trap exits with the original code, runner and sanitizer top-level handlers exit 1, the workflow retains set -e, and public cards remain status FAIL with no runtime-acceptance field.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The success evidence plan still requires exactly the same 40 static captures and does not accept dynamic operation names.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Moving the expected names into a shared contract accidentally drops an old capture or permits a dynamic private name.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Independent comparison proves CAPTURE_NAMES is exactly the old checker set; Lab.call rejects names outside it and the checker still requires set(named) equality plus all existing per-name semantic assertions.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Only the ten declared files change, all 841 joint source hashes bind the candidate tree, and P207 bytes remain unchanged.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: candidate index/tree, joint source_contract.json, and workflow pins
materialBoundaries.counterexample: An undeclared file, stale source hash, or P207 pin drift accompanies the diagnostic patch.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Manifest before/after bytes and blobs match; candidate index equals tree 3763f37; all 841 candidate-tree blobs match source_contract.json; the two P207 blobs equal base 747.

The underlying cause of run 41484652782 and the actual SKU remain UNKNOWN; this diagnostic patch does not fix or identify that business failure.
